decision.hypothesis: The recorded floor–payload penetration is the proximate state-qualification defect that prevented the native capability calculation from proceeding; paired local diagnostics of the same incomplete execution should reproduce that prerequisite failure without revealing an independent solver or finite-state defect.
decision.expected_observation: Both diagnostic repetitions identify the recorded floor–payload contact or associated contact-free state-support failure as the first qualification blocker and recover no separate finite-state, constraint-support, or solver-entry defect.
decision.weakening_observation: Either repetition reaches the same rejection while contact-free with finite supported state, or identifies an additional independent numerical, constraint-support, or solver-progress failure that would remain after removing the recorded contact.
decision.fixed_conditions: Use the exact saved candidate and incomplete native execution, frozen central_high reach task, standardized zero-state initialization, six tendon channels with 0–8 N bounds, 0.02 s control period, 0.6 s horizon, and the recorded native model assumptions. Do not alter design, task, controls, initial state, model, or acceptance criteria.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after the two prescribed diagnostic repetitions, or earlier if the diagnostic formally identifies an independent qualification blocker; do not infer task feasibility, infeasibility, or acceptance from this diagnostic.
decision.interpretation: This action distinguishes a contact-associated prerequisite rejection from a broader state-validity or numerical failure within the recorded execution. Reproduction would support only the contact-blocker mechanism for this attempt; it would not establish that removing contact makes the task feasible. A contact-free repeat with the same failure, or discovery of another blocker, would redirect the next investigation toward state support or solver progress rather than geometry alone.

decision.hypothesis: The incomplete nonlinear task-capability attempt was blocked by its numerical trajectory initialization entering payload-floor contact, rather than by demonstrated structural infeasibility; changing only the solver initialization to a bounded 0.2-to-0.4 N ramp may produce a finite, contact-free trajectory on which the same task-capability calculation can complete.
decision.expected_observation: The calculation reaches a completed numerical solve with finite, contact-free unconstrained states over the analyzed horizon and returns a scoped task-capability result instead of the prior state-support rejection. Any resulting margins remain model- and sample-scoped and require independent full replay for task acceptance.
decision.weakening_observation: The ramp-initialized calculation again encounters payload-floor contact, nonfinite state, or the same finite-contact-free-state requirement failure, or exhausts 120 iterations without a completed scoped result; this would weaken the initialization-basin explanation without establishing infeasibility.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep the exact candidate, frozen central_high task and standardized physical initial state, 0.6 s horizon, 0.02 s control period, six tendon channels in the recorded order, 0-8 N tension bounds, model representation, task-capability objective, and all physical parameters unchanged. Change only the numerical control-trajectory initialization from the prior attempt to the registered 0.2-to-0.4 N ramp; this is a solver seed and does not alter the frozen physical initial state.
decision.stopping_condition: End this single analysis when a completed scoped task-capability result is produced, when a finite/contact-free-state qualification failure is recorded, or after 120 iterations. Do not infer task acceptance, global feasibility, or structural infeasibility from this action alone.
decision.interpretation: The prior calculation recorded one payload-floor penetration of -0.00013816094441274768 m at 0.231 s and terminated as unqualified because it lacked a finite, contact-free unconstrained state. A same-candidate, same-objective calculation with a different solver seed directly tests whether that failure is sensitive to initialization. Successful completion would support further independent replay, not acceptance; repeated failure would localize the numerical/contact problem but would not exclude other trajectories or designs.
